source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Objectively estimate short-term mortality risk from liver disease, guiding organ allocation priority on a \"sickest first\" basis","B":"Determining a client's position on the waiting list based solely on how long they have already been waiting","C":"Applying mainly to clients with alcohol-related liver disease, rather than to clients with other causes of liver failure","D":"Carrying fairly little established relationship to how donor organs are actually allocated to waiting clients"}}
source_row.rationale: The MELD score objectively estimates short-term (3-month) mortality risk from liver disease, using lab values including creatinine, bilirubin, and INR (with MELD-Na also incorporating sodium), guiding organ allocation priority on a "sickest first" basis rather than time-based waiting, replacing the older Child-Pugh-based allocation system.
